key_insight: SeeEEG turns EEG signals into images, enabling a frozen vision foundation model to outperform specialized frozen EEG encoders across eight datasets.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support EEG analysis across clinical and sleep-related tasks, but these benchmarks do not establish readiness for clinical use.
method: Render each EEG channel as a waveform or scalogram in a dedicated row of image patches.
Optimize montage, filtering, and contrast through a frozen vision backbone using at most 1,113 trainable display parameters per view.
Compare frozen encoders using identical readout heads.
evidence_signal: Against seven EEG foundation models on eight datasets, SeeEEG with DINOv3 ViT-B achieved higher balanced accuracy than every comparator on all eight; random initialization reduced scores by 15.2 points on average.
watch_item: The results concern frozen-encoder benchmarks; performance against fully fine-tuned EEG models and in prospective clinical workflows remains unestablished.
paper_title: Your Vision Foundation Model Is Secretly an EEG Foundation Model
